name: UCB SA
overview: UCB SA is a Brussels-headquartered global biopharmaceutical company focused on severe diseases in immunology (dermatology, rheumatology) and neurology (epilepsy, myasthenia gravis), with roughly 16,000 employees across the U.S., Europe and Japan/international markets. The company generated EUR 7.7 billion of FY2025 revenue and is now led by its flagship immunology drug Bimzelx (bimekizumab), which alongside four other 'growth drivers' (Rystiggo, Zilbrysq, Fintepla, Evenity) is more than offsetting loss-of-exclusivity erosion in its legacy epilepsy franchise (Vimpat, Keppra, Briviact) and biosimilar-resistant Cimzia. UCB operates on a traditional branded-biopharma model: patent-protected biologics and small molecules sold to specialty pharmacies, hospitals and payers, supplemented by royalty income and a profit-share/royalty arrangement with Amgen/Astellas on Evenity.

business_model.summary: UCB earns the great majority of revenue from patented, mostly biologic (injectable) prescription medicines sold directly to healthcare systems and specialty/retail pharmacy channels in the U.S., Europe, Japan and international markets, supplemented by manufacturing/royalty income and a partnered profit contribution from Evenity (marketed by Amgen/Astellas outside Europe). Growth is now concentrated in five 'growth drivers' -- Bimzelx, Rystiggo, Zilbrysq, Fintepla and Evenity -- which grew from 39% of net sales in H1 2025 to 54% in H1 2026, offsetting loss-of-exclusivity (LOE) declines in Vimpat, Keppra and (from Feb-2026) Briviact. Revenue is transactional/prescription-driven rather than subscription-based, but has recurring, chronic-disease characteristics given long duration-of-therapy in epilepsy, myasthenia gravis and inflammatory skin/joint disease.

revenue_streams.name: Cimzia (certolizumab pegol - immunology)
revenue_streams.trend: flat/mature, LOE since 2024 but no biosimilar competition to date

revenue_streams.name: Briviact (brivaracetam - epilepsy)
revenue_streams.trend: declining - lost U.S. exclusivity Feb 2026, EU LOE expected Aug 2026

revenue_streams.name: Keppra/Vimpat (levetiracetam/lacosamide - epilepsy)
revenue_streams.trend: declining - legacy, generic erosion (Vimpat US LOE 2022, Japan generics from Dec 2025)

revenue_streams.name: Evenity (romosozumab - osteoporosis, partnered with Amgen/Astellas)
revenue_streams.trend: growing - Europe net sales plus worldwide profit-share booked in other operating income (EUR 379m H1 2026, +34%)

revenue_streams.name: Established brands (Neupro, Zyrtec, Xyzal) and royalties/contract manufacturing

business_model.customer_type: B2B/institutional - specialty pharmacies, hospitals, payers and health systems; end prescribers are dermatologists, rheumatologists and neurologists
business_model.geographic_mix_h1_2026: U.S. 62% (EUR 2,544m), Europe 24% (EUR 977m), International markets 9% (EUR 365m), Japan 4% (EUR 152m), of EUR 4,088m total net sales
business_model.recurring_vs_transactional: Transactional prescription sales with strong recurring characteristics given chronic-disease, multi-year treatment duration typical of epilepsy, myasthenia gravis and inflammatory skin/joint disease

main_competitors: Amgen (co-marketing partner on Evenity, also competes via other franchises)
competitive_position.market_position: Emerging leader/fast-follower in psoriasis, psoriatic arthritis, axial spondyloarthritis and hidradenitis suppurativa (HS) via Bimzelx; long-established but declining leadership in epilepsy; new entrant with meaningful share gains in generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) via Rystiggo/Zilbrysq, the only company with two approved gMG mechanisms.
competitive_position.market_share_notes: Bimzelx IL-17 'dynamic' new-patient share (per IQVIA data cited by UCB, June 2026): >35% in psoriasis, >30% in rheumatology (AS/nr-axSpA/PsA), ~45% in HS; approved in >50 countries with >135,000 patients treated worldwide as of mid-2026. However Bimzelx's overall installed-base share still trails incumbents Cosentyx, Taltz and Rinvoq, and Skyrizi/Tremfya (IL-23 class) remain far larger in absolute revenue -- AbbVie's Skyrizi and J&J's Tremfya generated roughly $17.6bn and $5.1bn respectively in the comparable period versus Bimzelx's EUR 2.2bn FY2025 net sales.

moat_factors.description: Bimzelx is the first and only approved dual IL-17A/IL-17F inhibitor and has now won four head-to-head superiority trials (BE RADIANT vs. secukinumab, BE VIVID, BE SURE vs. adalimumab, and BE BOLD vs. risankizumab in PsA on ACR50) -- a differentiated efficacy story versus IL-17 and IL-23 rivals, though translation into durable share gains against entrenched incumbents remains to be proven at scale

Company highlights U.S. patent protection out to 2033 (Rystiggo), 2035 (Zilbrysq) and 2037 (Bimzelx, assuming patent term extension is granted) -- an unusually long runway versus the recently-expired Cimzia/Vimpat/Briviact franchise

New U.S. biologics campus (Gwinnett County, Georgia) and expanded mammalian antibody/CMO network support in-house Bimzelx manufacturing and create a scale barrier, though this is a cost/execution advantage rather than a hard moat
Two distinct therapeutic-area franchises reduce single-indication concentration risk relative to narrower biotech peers

moat_factors.factor: Cimzia's Fc-free molecular structure / no biosimilar competition despite LOE
moat_factors.description: High barrier to entry (manufacturing complexity) has kept Cimzia biosimilar-free in the U.S. and EU more than two years after patent expiry, sustaining ~EUR 1.9bn/yr in sales longer than typical for a lost-exclusivity biologic
30-year epilepsy leadership underpins uptake of newer rare-epilepsy assets (Fintepla, Nayzilam) and rezanecel cell-therapy pipeline

weaknesses: Heavy and rising reliance on a single asset (Bimzelx) for growth -- any competitive, safety, or pricing setback would disproportionately hit the equity story
Legacy epilepsy franchise (Vimpat, Keppra, Briviact) is in structural decline from generic/LOE erosion, requiring the growth drivers to keep outrunning a shrinking base
Bimzelx access/reimbursement still lags established IL-17s (Cosentyx, Taltz) in some markets, and management explicitly flags 'net pricing erosion' as access expands
Smaller scale than mega-cap immunology competitors (AbbVie, J&J, Novartis, Lilly) with larger sales forces and broader portfolios
Evenity economics are shared with Amgen/Astellas (royalty/profit-share only outside Europe), capping UCB's capture of that franchise's upside

growth_drivers: Bimzelx global uptake and new-indication expansion: peak sales guidance raised to 'at least EUR 7 billion' (from prior lower guidance), with pediatric/adolescent HS and psoriasis trials underway, palmoplantar pustulosis (PPP) launch expected, and ongoing indication broadening across PsA, axSpA/AS and HS

Generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) franchise: Rystiggo (rozanolixizumab, FcRn inhibitor) and Zilbrysq (zilucoplan, C5 complement inhibitor) are the only dual-mechanism gMG portfolio on the market; new Phase 3 studies expanding into ocular MG and MOGAD
Evenity royalty/profit-share contribution growing 34-41% YoY (EUR 379m H1 2026), a high-margin, low-capex income stream
Fintepla expansion beyond Dravet/Lennox-Gastaut into CDKL5 deficiency disorder (filed with FDA/EMA in 2026) and Rett syndrome (Phase 3 initiated)

Pipeline/business-development escalation: 2026 acquisitions of Candid Therapeutics (T-cell engager platform, up to $2.2bn, cizutamig lead asset) and Neurona Therapeutics (rezanecel cell therapy for epilepsy, up to $1.15bn) add next-generation immune-reset and disease-modification modalities across immunology and neurology

Late-stage pipeline optionality: dapirolizumab pegol (lupus, partnered with Biogen), galvokimig (dual IL-13/IL-17A/F, atopic dermatitis and respiratory), bepranemab (anti-tau, Alzheimer's, FDA Fast Track), STACCATO alprazolam (seizure rescue)
KYGEVVI (TK2 deficiency) approval broadens the ultra-rare disease portfolio
U.S. biologics manufacturing expansion (new Georgia campus) supporting Bimzelx and future launches

business.description: Bimzelx is now UCB's single largest product (EUR 2.2bn FY2025, EUR 1.5bn in H1 2026 alone, ~37% of net sales) and the primary driver of the equity re-rating; any clinical, safety, access or competitive setback would have an outsized impact on both fundamentals and the multiple

Entrenched incumbents Cosentyx (Novartis) and Taltz (Lilly) still outperform Bimzelx on ease of access; IL-23 leaders Skyrizi (AbbVie) and Tremfya (J&J) are far larger in absolute revenue and well-resourced to defend share

Briviact lost U.S. exclusivity in February 2026 (EU LOE expected August 2026); Vimpat sales down -41% actual in H1 2026 on Japan generic entry (Dec 2025); Keppra facing generic erosion in Japan under new 'Elective Care Scheme'
No biosimilar competition to date (LOE in U.S. Feb 2024, EU Oct 2024, Japan 2026) due to manufacturing complexity, but this remains a standing risk to a ~EUR 1.9bn/yr revenue line

Two debt-funded acquisitions closed in H1 2026 (Candid, Neurona) plus the IMIDomics data-business purchase; purchase price allocations were not yet finalized as of June 2026, and pipeline integration/execution risk is elevated

financial.description: UCB moved from a EUR 7m net cash position at Dec-2025 to EUR 2.8bn net debt at June-2026 (0.8x net debt/adjusted EBITDA) after funding Candid and Neurona partly via a $1.5bn bullet term loan and a EUR 150m revolving credit draw; net financial expenses expected to rise further

~62% of net sales are U.S.-dollar denominated; management guides to roughly -2 percentage points revenue and -6 percentage points adjusted EBITDA growth impact if 30-June-2026 FX rates persist for FY2026

financial.risk: Gross margin pressure from access expansion
financial.description: Management explicitly flagged that 'improving access comes with pricing pressure expected to impact FY gross margin' for Bimzelx and other growth drivers

regulatory.risk: U.S. drug pricing reform / IRA Medicare negotiation
regulatory.description: Ongoing U.S. policy uncertainty around Medicare drug price negotiation (IRA) and a proposed 'Most Favored Nation' (MFN) executive order that would tie U.S. list prices to lower international reference prices; UCB's FY2026 guidance explicitly excludes any potential impact of U.S. tariffs or an MFN pricing arrangement given no final outcome has been determined
Evolving U.S. trade policy includes proposed pharmaceutical tariffs; financial impact not yet quantifiable per management's own H1-2026 disclosure
Ongoing risk that biosimilar competitors eventually enter for Cimzia despite the currently high manufacturing barrier to entry

macro.description: Fed held rates at 3.50-3.75% through mid-2026 in a 'higher-for-longer' stance; ECB raised rates 25bp in June 2026 (first hike since 2023) amid resurgent inflation -- raises the cost of UCB's new acquisition-related debt

Ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East cited by management as contributing to supply chain and inflation volatility, though UCB states limited direct commercial footprint in affected regions

execution.description: UCB shares have re-rated dramatically over the past several years (52-week range roughly EUR 181-290 during 2026) as Bimzelx execution has repeatedly beaten expectations; the current price already embeds substantial further Bimzelx success (peak sales now guided 'at least EUR 7bn'), leaving limited room for disappointment and significant multiple-compression risk if growth decelerates

Several next-generation pipeline bets (bepranemab in Alzheimer's, galvokimig in atopic dermatitis/COPD, cizutamig in autoimmune T-cell engagement, rezanecel cell therapy) are early-stage and unproven at scale; TOGETHER proof-of-concept study for bepranemab missed its primary endpoint in the overall population (signal only in a low-tau subgroup)

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global immunology (IL-17/IL-23 class) and neurology/rare-disease biopharma markets continue to grow at high-single to double-digit rates, driven by underdiagnosis/undertreatment in dermatology and rheumatology, aging-related bone health, and expanding biologic use in myasthenia gravis; UCB frames itself as entering 'a decade of expected growth' across all regions
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low - biopharmaceutical demand for chronic/severe disease treatment is largely non-discretionary and non-cyclical, though reimbursement/formulary dynamics and government budget pressure can affect net pricing
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate - historically net-cash/near-net-cash balance sheet turned net-debt (EUR 2.8bn, 0.8x EBITDA) after 2026 acquisitions, increasing sensitivity to rates on the new term loan and RCF draw
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Material - approximately 62% of net sales are USD-denominated (reported in EUR); Japanese yen exposure is smaller but also hedged; FY2026 guidance flags meaningful FX drag on both revenue and EBITDA growth at recent exchange rates
key_input_costs: Biologics manufacturing capacity (mammalian cell culture, fill-finish)
R&D/clinical trial costs (R&D was 24% of FY2025 revenue)
macro_factors.regulatory_environment_trend: Increasingly complex U.S. pricing policy (IRA Medicare negotiation, proposed MFN pricing, tariff threats) creates headline and margin risk industry-wide; EU HTA reform and biosimilar policy are secondary considerations

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue EUR 4,270m (+22%, +27% CER), net sales EUR 4,088m (+23%, +28% CER), adjusted EBITDA EUR 1,736m (+68%, +79% CER) at a 40.7% margin (vs. 29.6% H1 2025), profit more than doubled to EUR 1,111m, core EPS EUR 6.84 (vs. EUR 3.53)

FY2026 guidance raised for the second time: revenue growth raised to low-teens to mid-teens % CER (from high single-digit to low double-digit %); adjusted EBITDA growth raised to mid-teens to low-twenties % CER (from high single-digit to mid-teens %); guidance explicitly excludes potential U.S. tariff or MFN pricing impacts

Bimzelx peak sales guidance raised to 'at least EUR 7 billion', citing >135,000 patients treated worldwide, approval in >50 countries, and IL-17 dynamic new-patient share of >35% in psoriasis, >30% in rheumatology and ~45% in HS (per IQVIA data through May 2026)

BE BOLD head-to-head Phase 3 study (presented at EULAR 2026) showed Bimzelx superiority over AbbVie's Skyrizi (IL-23 inhibitor) on ACR50 in psoriatic arthritis -- UCB's fourth head-to-head superiority win (after BE RADIANT vs. secukinumab, BE VIVID vs. ustekinumab/placebo, BE SURE vs. adalimumab)

Completed acquisition of Neurona Therapeutics (up to $1.15bn: $650m upfront + up to $500m milestones), adding rezanecel, a Phase 1/2 GABAergic interneuron cell therapy for drug-resistant mesial temporal lobe epilepsy, partly funded by a new $1.5bn bullet term loan

Completed acquisition of Candid Therapeutics (up to $2.2bn: $2.0bn upfront + up to $200m milestones), adding cizutamig (BCMA x CD3 T-cell engager) and a broader T-cell-engager platform across >10 autoimmune indications
Acquired the Patient Insight Business of IMIDomics, adding curated immunology datasets to accelerate precision-driven drug discovery

European Commission granted marketing authorization under exceptional circumstances for KYGEVVI (TK2 deficiency) -- the first approved treatment for this ultra-rare mitochondrial disease; also filed Fintepla for CDKL5 deficiency disorder with FDA and EMA
Briviact (brivaracetam) lost U.S. market exclusivity, exposing the product to generic competition; European LOE expected August 2026

FY2025 results: revenue EUR 7,741m (+26%, +29% CER), adjusted EBITDA EUR 2,636m (+79% reported, margin 34% of revenue, or 31.4% excluding one-offs); Bimzelx FY2025 net sales EUR 2,227m; balance sheet was net cash of EUR 7m at year-end 2025 (pre-acquisition)
Balance-sheet swing from net cash to net debt (EUR 2.8bn, 0.8x EBITDA) by mid-2026 following debt-funded M&A, a EUR 276m dividend payment and EUR 127m of treasury share buybacks in H1 2026

guidance.as_of: H1 2026 Results (30 July 2026), superseding FY2025 guidance issued 26 February 2026

items.notes: Raised from prior guidance of high single-digit % to low double-digit % (which itself was raised from the original FY2025-issued guidance); driven by strong performance of the five growth drivers and BIMZELX access expansion, partly offset by net pricing erosion and Briviact LOE
Raised from high single-digit % to mid-teens %; on an adjusted basis excluding 2025 one-offs, growth guided at mid-twenties % to low-thirties % (raised from high teens % to mid-twenties %)
Reflects sustained use of R&D tax incentives and deferred tax asset recognition on losses

items.target: Approximately -2 percentage points to revenue growth; approximately -6 percentage points to adjusted EBITDA growth
items.notes: If 30-June-2026 exchange rates persist for the remainder of the year; primarily USD and JPY exposure
Raised on the back of accelerating global uptake, >135,000 patients treated, and expanding indication set (5 approved indications, pediatric/PPP expansion underway)

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Jean-Christophe Tellier and CFO Sandrine Dufour framed H1 2026 as 'strong performance' with guidance raised for the second consecutive period, citing the five growth drivers (now >50% of net sales, up from 39% a year earlier) and the EVENITY profit contribution. Management explicitly cautioned that 'improving access comes with pricing pressure expected to impact FY gross margin' for BIMZELX, and that R&D expense is expected to increase in H2 2026 including the impact of the Candid and Neurona acquisitions. Guidance excludes any potential impact from U.S. tariffs or a Most Favoured Nation (MFN) pricing arrangement, as no final outcomes had been determined as of the report date.

valuation_context.note: UCB shares have re-rated very strongly over the past several years on the back of repeated Bimzelx-driven earnings beats and guidance raises. The stock's 52-week range during 2026 has spanned roughly EUR 181-290, and multi-year performance shows the shares up well over 100% versus five years ago. At the stated current price of EUR 216.50, the shares sit meaningfully below their 2026 highs but still reflect a substantial premium re-rating versus UCB's historical trading range prior to Bimzelx's commercial inflection. Given that FY2026 guidance already assumes low-teens-to-mid-teens revenue growth and mid-teens-to-low-twenties adjusted EBITDA growth, and BIMZELX peak sales guidance has been raised to 'at least EUR 7 billion,' the market is likely already pricing in substantial further Bimzelx commercial success. Investors should treat consensus estimates and any DCF/valuation work on this name as sitting atop several years of beat-and-raise momentum, with correspondingly less room for error before multiple compression risk becomes material.

bull_case: Bimzelx has repeatedly beaten expectations and won four head-to-head superiority trials against major incumbents (adalimumab, ustekinumab/placebo, secukinumab, risankizumab), supporting durable share gains and a raised peak sales target of at least EUR 7 billion

Five growth drivers (Bimzelx, Rystiggo, Zilbrysq, Fintepla, Evenity) now generate more than half of net sales and are compounding at 20-90%+ CER, more than offsetting the structural decline of the legacy epilepsy/Cimzia franchise

Long patent runway disclosed by management (U.S. exclusivity to 2033 for Rystiggo, 2035 for Zilbrysq, potentially 2037 for Bimzelx) provides an unusually long growth horizon versus a typical biopharma portfolio
Operating leverage is substantial: adjusted EBITDA margin expanded from 29.6% to 40.7% year-over-year in H1 2026 as the growth drivers scale against a largely fixed cost base

2026 acquisitions (Candid's T-cell engager platform, Neurona's cell therapy) add next-generation, potentially disease-modifying modalities in both immunology and neurology, extending the growth runway beyond the current five-drug cohort
bear_case: The stock has already re-rated to reflect substantial future Bimzelx success -- FY2026 guidance and the raised EUR 7bn+ peak sales target mean continued outperformance is now the baseline expectation, not upside, leaving limited margin for disappointment

Bimzelx faces well-capitalized, entrenched competition (Cosentyx, Taltz, Skyrizi, Tremfya) with superior current access in some markets, and management itself flags 'net pricing erosion' as access expands -- growth may increasingly come at the expense of price

Legacy franchise erosion is accelerating: Briviact lost U.S. exclusivity in February 2026 (EU to follow August 2026), Vimpat sales fell -41% in H1 2026 on Japan generic entry, and Cimzia's multi-year biosimilar-free run could end at any time

The company swung from EUR 7m net cash to EUR 2.8bn net debt within six months to fund the Candid and Neurona acquisitions, adding financial leverage and integration risk just as U.S. drug-pricing policy (potential MFN referencing, tariffs) introduces unquantified downside that management has explicitly excluded from guidance

Roughly 62% of net sales are USD-denominated against EUR reporting; management's own guidance flags a potential -2pt revenue and -6pt EBITDA growth FX drag if rates persist, and reported EPS quality is already sensitive to large amortization/one-off adjustments (Core EPS vs. GAAP EPS)
